full_judgment:
2. The plaintiff/decree-holder filed a Money Suit against the defendant Bank and others for recovery of an amount of Tk. 97,750/-. The suit was decreed in the following terms: 

 "That the suit be decreed on contest against the defendants 1-3 with costs and ex-parte against the rest without costs. The plaintiff do get Tk. 97,750/- with interest @ 15% per annum till realisation." 

 3. The petitioner filed an application in the said Money Suit stating that the plaintiff has not filed any Execution Case against the defendants but the defendants pray for directing the Court to deposit Taka 1,07,095/- through challan for satisfaction of the decree. The trial Court by Order No. 64 dated 13.11.86 allowed the prayer and directed the judgment-debtor to deposit the amount through challan and the defendant petitioner deposited the amount on 15.11.86 by challan No. 6241. By Order No. 66 dated 23.12.86 the Court permitted the plaintiff to draw the amount and the money was withdrawn by the plaintiff. Thereafter the decree-holder filed the Execution case for recovery of Tk. 76,361.25 as interest @ 15% for the period from the institution of the suit till realisation. 

 4. Main contention of the petitioner is that reading of the decree shows that the interest is to be paid from the date of decree and not from the date of institution of the suit and hence the trial Court acted wrongly in proceeding with Execution Case. The impugned orders show that the Execution Court is-sued order of attachment in pursuance of the decree and refused to stay the execution of the decree as prayed for by the petitioner. 

 5. A counter affidavit has been filed by the opposite party No. 1 stating that the plaintiff filed the suit and prayed for a decree of an ascertained amount of sum namely 97,750/- against the defendant Bank along with cost and interest pendente life till realisation of the decrial amount @ 15% per annum. Ac-cording to the opposite party the Court has decreed the suit in terms of the prayer and as such the petitioner has wrongly calculated the interest from the date of the decree which in fact will be calculated from the date of the filing of the suit till realisation. In the counter affidavit it has also been stated that the defendant No. 1 Bank has already deposited the balance amount of interest of Tk. 76,361.25 paisa from the date of filing of the suit vide pay order No. 505373 dated 5.7.87 and the said amount is lying be-fore the Executing Court. It has also been stated that there is no certificate of full satisfaction of the decree by the Executing Court. 

 6. The short point involved in this Rule is whether the interest as awarded by the trial Court is to be calculated from the date of decree or from the date of institution of the suit. 

 7. Mr. Asrarul Hossain, the learned advocate appearing for the petitioner firstly submits that as per section 34 of the Code of Civil Procedure no interest has been specifically granted from the date of filing of suit and as such execution of the interest pending litigation is illegal. Secondly, he argues that a certificate of satisfaction of the decree having been granted, the execution case is liable to be dismissed and the same cannot be re-opened and proceeded in law. 

 8. Mr. Shafique Ahmed, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of opposite party No. I submits that the decree has been passed in the present case as per the relief claimed from the date of filing of the suit till realisation and there being no ambiguity in the decree as such the learned Advocate for the petitioner wrongly interpreted that the interest has been refused from the date of filing of the suit. 

 9. A reference to section 34 C.P.C. shows that it is the discretion of the Court to grant interest and the Court may grant 3 kinds of interest istly court cant grant interest from the date of the suit to the date of the decree. The award of interest under this section after the date of filling of the suit is entirely a matter of discretion of Court. This purely is a matter of statutory power. In a decree for the payment of money, the Court may pass an order of interest at such rate as the Court deems reasonable to be paid on the principal sum adjudged, from the date of the suit to the date of the decree. In the present case the relief that was sought for, is one of interest pendente the till realisation of the decretal amount @ 15% per annum. The trial court decreed the suit awarding the interest @ 15% per annum till realisation. Normally in such suit when the claim is pending litigation the court al-lows such interest unless of course on the contrary a very sufficient cause for not awarding interest is made out. Mr. Hossain's main contention is that the decree has not specifically mentioned that the interest is to be paid from the date of the filing of suit and that is why it should be read as awarded from the date of the decree. This is not a case where the decree is totally silent with regard to the interest but interest has been awarded in the suit with 15% per annum till realisation. Thus it is difficult for us to hold that the interest has been refused from the date of filing of the suit. The other two kinds of interest which the Court may grant in a case under section 34 C.P.C. are interest for the period prior to the institution of the suit. This is, of course, a matter of substantive law and is outside the purview of the section and next the Court can award interest for the period after passing of the decree till the payment of sum due. Section 34(2) of the Code of course speaks of further interest on such aggregate sum from the date of decree, to the date of payment or other earlier date. Thus it appears to us that as regards interest from the date of the suit however the position is different and the matter is covered by Section 34 Which gives complete discretion to the court to sward pendente lite interest. In the present case the trial court had adjudged the principal sum and has ordered for payment of interest 15% per annum till realisation. Mr. Hossain has submitted four decisions for our consideration. Firstly, he cited a case reported in 1940 (Madras), 29. That was a case, where decree is silent with respect to the payment of further interest from the date of the decree to the date of payment and the decree follows the Judgment, the Court must be deemed to have refused it. 

 In that reported decision nothing was stated in the Judgment with regard to the payment of further interest after the date of the decree. That was a case under Sub-Section (2) of Section 34. In that decision it was observed like this: 

 "Section 34(I) provides that where and in so far as a decree is for the payment of money the Court may, award further interest, but sub-sec. (2) expressly states that where a decree is silent with respect to the payment of further interest from the date of the decree to the date of payment or other earlier date, the Court shall be deemed to have refused such interest, and a separate suit therefore shall not lie." 

 Thus this case is not of much help in the present case. A.I.R. 1937 (Madras) 511 is a case where "Once a decree-holder has admitted payment by Judgment-debtor he cannot be allowed to execute his decree for same amount over again." 

 The reported decision is case of constructive res Judicata. A.I.R. 1931 (Madras) 650 is a case where it has been held that the Executing Court can-not allow interest when decree is silent as to interest. 

 10. Thus this case is also not of any help to us in deciding the present case. Another case cited is 3 B.C.R. 1983 (HCD) 339. That was a case with regard to payment of further interest-on the aggregate sum from the date of decree to the date of payment and in that reported decision the decree being silent, Court held that interest is deemed to have been refused. Thus the four decisions cited by the learned Advocate for the petitioner are not very relevant in the facts of the present case. 

 11. The learned Advocate for the Opposite Party also cited the case of M/S. M.M. Ispahani Vs. Sonali Bank and Ors. reported in 1985 D.L.R. (A.D.)l. The learned Advocate submits that in that reported decision a decree was passed in the following terms a decree for Tk. 6,31,10,307.13 with interest thereon at the rate of 12% per annum till realisation." The learned Judges of the Appellate Division at paragraph 8 observed as follows: 

 13. From Order No. 1 it appears that the execution case was started on 23.12.86. Before starting of the execution case the defendant filed an application on 13.11.86 before the trial Court in the money suit for putting the detrital amount suo moto as per decree on his own calculation. So in reality the execution case has not started as per provision of Order 21 of the Code of Civil Procedure and before starting of the execution case the money was deposited. Thus factually it cannot be said that the executing Court has granted the certificate of satisfaction in the execution case at all. In the present case the judgment was passed on 26.8.86 and the decree was drawn on 4.9.86 and the petitioner filed an application on 13.11.86 for deposit of money in the suit itself according to his own calculation. Thus both the points of the learned Advocate for the petitioner fail.
